summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with right leg cellulitis and fever after incomplete response to oral antibiotics. He was started on IV vancomycin, which was adjusted based on trough levels. Imaging ruled out DVT and fractures. His infection improved during the short hospital stay, and he was discharged home with a plan to complete a 10-day course of IV vancomycin during dialysis sessions. He was advised to continue all home medications, including those for gout, coronary artery disease, and hypertension, and to follow up with his primary care provider regarding medication adherence.
